title: Prioritize small payloads and graceful fallbacks for streaming tool/function calls in gateway
author: Priya Menon
description:
Context: Production customers observed increased tail latency for short tool/function-calling requests when the gateway was co-located with large batched generation workloads. This PR updates routing and proxy buffer policies so small payload, low-token-rate requests (typical in fncall workflows) are prioritized onto low-latency routes and are protected from head-of-line blocking.

What I changed: - Added a route-priority rule that scores requests by (payload_bytes, expected_stream_rate, route_health) and prefers nodes with low existing KV-cache pressure. - Introduced a soft payload limit (route-specific soft_limit_bytes) enforced at the gateway with a backoff policy; requests exceeding the soft limit get a 413-soft response header suggesting chunking, and are forwarded to larger-capacity routes instead of being dropped. - Streaming proxy: replaced fixed 256KB per-client in-memory buffer with an adaptive low-water/high-water window that keeps at most 32KB of eager buffer for low-rate streams and allows opportunistic burst buffering for large streams up to route hard limit. This reduces memory pressure and reduces blocking of small fncall streams. - Fncall/OpenAI-compat handshake: tightened the initial stream-framing timeout to 7s (was 15s) with an opt-out flag for customers on high-latency links. This prevents stuck handshakes from tying up proxy resources. - Added compatibility shim so OpenAI-compatible requests that use structured toolcall semantics get routed to nodes with structured-output validators enabled. - Instrumentation: added metrics (gateway.small_payload_route_hit, streaming.buffer_window_ms, stream.handshake_timeouts) and dashboards, plus an alert on small_payload_route_miss_rate > 2%.

Why: Fixes multiple customer incidents where quick tool calls experienced 3-10x higher p95 latency under mixed workloads. The new behavior preserves OpenAI-compatible surface semantics while improving median and tail latency for short synchronous tool calls.

Rollout: Feature guarded behind gateway feature-flag (gate.priority_small_payloads). Default off for dedicated/private until validated. Gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% in hosted over 72 hours with monitoring gating.

Notes: This is focused on surface-level routing and proxy buffer behavior only; no model-serving runtime changes.

review_thread: Ava Liu: Can you add a guard so this doesn't trigger for private deployments by default? (requested change)
Author (Priya Menon): Added feature flag and updated docs to mark default off for private/dedicated. PTAL.
Diego Martinez: The new handshake timeout seems aggressive; can we make it configurable per-region? (requested change)
Author: Made timeout configurable via route_schema.yaml with per-region override and added integration test for handshake opt-out flag.
Sasha Ivanov: Approve. Verified metrics and dashboard look reasonable in staging.
Ava Liu: Approve after flag and docs update.
motivation: Reduce p95/p99 latency for short toolcalls and structured-output streams by preventing head-of-line blocking at the gateway and providing predictable fallbacks for oversized payloads.
ci_flaky_notes: Integration had a transient failure related to proxy handshake jitter in CI; rerun passed. Marking test as flaky tracked in ENG-1582.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misclassification could route high-throughput requests to small-route nodes causing saturation. Mitigation: soft-limit decision is conservative, reroutes to larger-capacity routes, and rollout gating/alerts will catch regressions.
deployment_plan: Gate the feature behind gate.priority_small_payloads. Deploy to hosted 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72h with monitoring->rollback on alert. Dedicated/private off by default; customers can opt-in via console or route config.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on scoring heuristics and the handshake timeout default. Pay attention to the integration test simulating mixed small/large concurrent streams.
